lines: - **Switching tabs just shows the list.** The ALL, DAILY, MAIN and MISC tabs, and ACTIVE / COMPLETED, no longer slide or fade the list in: your quests are simply there. Opening and closing a quest's subtasks (zooming in and out) still slides, so you keep your bearings.
- **Everything you press answers the moment your finger lands,** before you let go:
- tabs, filter chips and the TRASH / CLEAR… buttons light their frames;
- UNDO, ✕ and the breadcrumb's links brighten;
- the ACTIVE / COMPLETED switch lights its bar.
- **A quest you hold lights up,** so you can see the hold registering before it lifts for dragging or opens its menu. A quick scroll never flashes the rows it passes.

- **Fixed: the app slowed down after opening COMPLETED,** the more so the more you've completed. Coming back to your quests no longer prepares your whole completed history out of sight, so ticking, typing and switching stay quick, however long your history.
- **Settings, Help, What's new and Trash open faster,** and closing them is quicker too: the main screen behind them no longer redraws.
- **Ticking boxes and searching are quicker with lots of completed quests.**

- **Tabs switch at once.** The tab you tap lights up the moment you tap it, and its list follows right after. Tap several tabs quickly and you land on the last one. The same goes for ACTIVE and COMPLETED.
- **Snappier all round:**
- lists open faster: rows no longer prepare their animations in advance (the strikethrough, the checkbox pop, the +XP, the swipe tracks); each one is built when it plays;
- starting to edit a title is quicker;
- typing in a title, ticking boxes and swiping do less work behind the scenes.
- **A shorter top panel,** so more of your list fits on the screen:
- the ALL, DAILY, MAIN and MISC tabs are half as tall, with the name and its count on one line;
- the line under the title (ACTIVE · DONE TODAY · streak) is gone;
- the **?** button moved into Settings: the user guide is under HELP there.

- **The top panel's scanlines move, gently,** as on the desktop: they drift slowly down, and every 7 seconds a soft band of light passes down the panel. They move only while the main screen is showing, and they stay still with Reduce Motion on. The drift moves a pixel at a time, a few times a second, so it costs very little battery.
- **Fixed: closing a quest near the end of the list sometimes nudged it** by a few points. It now stays exactly where it is.
